dimensions.name: Problem & algorithm orientation

evidence.note: Lists networks with sizes and inspects the reference alignment before acting — characterizing both instances and the exploitable reference signal.
Validates/scores the reference alignment with a scoring script, checks tooling, and computes degree statistics — quantitative characterization of degree distribution and sizes.
Chooses and implements SANA (Simulated Annealing Network Aligner) in sana.c, a known published S3-optimizing method — a deliberate, known-reasonable algorithm selection.
Runs separate DM-HS S3/temp sweeps vs yeast 'ncw' (node-correctness-weight) runs, showing awareness that NC (via reference) and S3 (topology) are distinct per-deliverable levers.
Adds degree-seeded init and reference-guided moves, exploiting the reference alignment as a signal for the NC-constrained yeast deliverable.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent systematically characterized each network pair (sizes, format, degree stats) and the reference alignment, then implemented a specific published method (SANA) with reference-guided/NC-weighted variants tailored per deliverable — matching the level-8 anchor's 'characterize + research concrete methods + notice task-specific levers (name/reference for NC, topology for S3).' It stops short of 10 because there is no visible comparison of multiple published methods against instance runtime and no explicit naive-baseline score quantification before committing.

dimensions.name: Pipeline decomposition & thresholds as milestones

evidence.note: Front-loaded understanding stage: network sizes, reference alignment inspection, degree stats — a distinct sub-goal before building anything.

Scorer built THEN validated by scoring the provided reference alignment first — a done-check tying the metric implementation to the thresholds before an aligner exists; correct sequencing (scorer before optimizer).
Baseline aligner milestone: TaskCreate 'Build C aligner', write sana.c, compile, short test run + verify scoring — a gated checkpoint before optimization.
Yeast deliverable saved/verified and 'locked = ya3' once its S3/NC targets were met, treating the two deliverables as separate milestones with their own thresholds.
After locking yeast, effort is budgeted overwhelmingly toward the harder S3-only DM-HS target (250+ steps of optimization), showing difficulty-weighted allocation across deliverables.
'Save fallback DM-HS and validate' and 'Save z1 fallback' — preserving validated intermediate results as fallback branches while continuing to optimize.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent exhibits the full level-8 pattern: explicit ordered milestones (understand → scorer validated against reference → baseline aligner verified → optimize to numeric thresholds), each with a concrete done-check and sensibly sequenced (the scorer is validated before the optimizer is built). It exceeds pure level-8 by budgeting effort across the two deliverables by difficulty (yeast locked at step 118 once targets met, then ~250 steps devoted to the harder DM-HS S3 goal) and by keeping validated fallback saves (steps 106, 256, 376) with gating on measured scores before advancing. It stops just short of a fully crisp per-milestone fallback hierarchy, so 9 rather than 10.

dimensions.name: Self-scoring against the specified metrics

evidence.note: Builds a scoring script then 'Validate reference alignment and score it' — scores the known-perfect reference alignment, the canonical level-8 sanity check to confirm NC≈1.0 and a sensible S3 before trusting the scorer.
'Short test run and verify scoring' — cross-checks the aligner's reported score against the independent scorer early, establishing the scorer as the trusted feedback loop.

'Drift check' → fix → 'Re-check drift after fix' — verifies the incremental/delta score matches full recompute, exactly the guard against off-by-one/edge-double-counting bugs described in the level-10 anchor.
Repeated correctness verifications of move operators (imgdeg, guided swap, degree-aware swap) ensure the objective stays faithful as the code changes.
'Save and verify yeast alignment' and 'Save fallback DM-HS and validate' — validation of saved output alignments (coverage/injectivity/format) before treating them as submittable.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent implemented an independent scorer, sanity-checked it by scoring the provided reference alignment (step 12), verified the aligner's internal score against it (step 27), and used the score as the optimization objective throughout every batch. It also ran drift checks confirming incremental deltas match full recompute (215-219) and validated move-operator correctness and saved alignments — behavior spanning the level-8 anchor (reference-scored, faithful, objective-driven) and touching the level-10 guard against delta double-counting bugs. I hold at 8 rather than higher because the evidence is limited to descriptive step titles, so I cannot fully confirm exact format/node-name-spec verification or the literal faithfulness of the S3/E2_aligned denominator implementation.

dimensions.name: Score-tracking across optimization

evidence.note: Builds a scoring script and validates/scores the reference alignment first, establishing a ground-truth measurement baseline before optimizing.
Repeatedly captures full 'trajectory' of a run's score progression, indicating logging of score-over-time rather than isolated point checks.
Consistent 'mid-check' of long background runs across the whole horizon — monitors whether optimization is still gaining vs plateaued.
Preserves best-so-far per deliverable ('Lock yeast=ya3', 'Save fallback DM-HS and validate', 'Save p3', 'Save z1 fallback') while continuing to explore — the hallmark of the 10 anchor.
Constant-T / equilibrium probes used to diagnose whether the search is stuck vs converging, informing decisions to switch strategy.
Distance-to-threshold awareness ('yeast ncw push', 'yeast margin runs') targeting NC and margin above S3 targets.

dimensions.reasoning: Across a 386-step optimization the agent maintains a scoring harness, repeatedly logs per-run score trajectories, does mid-run checks on long batches, and — most tellingly — locks and saves named best-so-far fallback alignments (ya3, p3, z1) while exploring new variants, then switches approaches after plateaus diagnosed via equilibrium probes. This matches the 8-10 band (best-so-far tracking, plateau recognition, preserving best while exploring, no evidence of losing the plot). I hold at 9 rather than 10 because the log exposes only step descriptions, so I cannot fully confirm the numeric fidelity of the tracking.

dimensions.name: Strategy revision when thresholds aren't met

evidence.note: Uses a node-correctness-weight ('ncw') push specifically for the yeast deliverable (which has the NC>=0.30 constraint), then locks yeast=ya3 once satisfied — deliberately exploiting the reference/NC signal for one constraint set and freezing that gain.

When DM-HS (pure S3 topological constraint) plateaus, introduces a sequence of materially different tactics: degree-seeded initialization, guided topological moves, constant-T equilibrium probes, and iterated SA reheat — not seed reruns but algorithmic changes.
Diagnoses a 'drift' correctness bug in the incremental scoring, fixes it, and re-checks — evidence-driven correction rather than grinding a broken objective.

Continued distinct pivots on the lagging S3 metric: tournament selection, decaying pGuide (pGuideEff), and degree-aware guiding (DEGAW=3), each preceded by a short test before committing to long batches.
Repeatedly saves best-so-far fallbacks (fallback DM-HS, p3, z1) while probing new variants — abandons dead ends without discarding accumulated gains.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent treats the two constraint sets with complementary signals — reference/name-overlap weighting for the yeast NC target and pure topological/local-search machinery for the DM-HS S3 target — and pivots deliberately when a metric lags, matching anchor 8. It runs a long chain of genuinely different tactics (degree seeding, guided moves, reheat, tournament, decaying/degree-aware guiding, degree-aware swap) each prompted by observed plateaus, while preserving best-so-far fallbacks. It falls short of 10 because much of the late trajectory is repetitive polling of long runs and I cannot see explicit hypothesis-forming prose in the observations, so the crisp 'form hypothesis → test → abandon' rhythm is inferred rather than fully evidenced.

rubric.task_read: An open-ended global network-alignment optimization task: produce two injective node mappings between PPI networks that clear specified S3 (topological) and NC (node-correctness) thresholds. The horizon is long and the difficulty is real — hitting the numeric targets likely requires researching/implementing a nontrivial alignment algorithm (e.g., seed-and-extend, IsoRank/SANA/MAGNA-style), plus building the S3/NC metrics locally since the metrics are fully specified but the grader is hidden. A skilled practitioner would invest heavily in research, self-verification, and iterative optimization; the two deliverables have different constraints (one needs NC against a provided reference), so approaches may diverge.

dimensions.name: Problem & algorithm orientation
dimensions.description: Inspecting the graph files/sizes and the reference alignment, and researching/selecting a suitable network-alignment approach before committing.
dimensions.why_it_matters: S3/NC thresholds are hard to hit with a naive mapping; the space of alignment algorithms is well-studied, and the provided reference alignment plus node-name overlap are exploitable signals. Acting blind almost guarantees thrash.

anchors.0: Starts writing a mapping with no look at graph sizes, file format, or the reference alignment; no consideration of what algorithm could work.
anchors.3: Skims one file and picks an arbitrary heuristic (e.g., degree-sort or random injective map) without weighing whether it can clear the thresholds.
anchors.5: Reads both network pairs (sizes, format, node-name conventions), inspects the reference alignment, and picks a known-reasonable approach (seed-and-extend, IsoRank, or an existing tool) with a stated rationale.
anchors.8: Systematically characterizes each pair (|V|,|E|, degree distribution, shared node names), researches concrete alignment methods and their fit to S3 vs NC, and notices task-specific levers (name-overlap for NC, topology for S3; differing constraints per deliverable) that shape the plan.
anchors.10: Deep, sustained orientation: quantifies what score a baseline achieves, identifies the exact structural signal each threshold rewards, evaluates multiple published methods against the concrete instance sizes/runtime, and derives a targeted strategy per deliverable grounded in that analysis.

dimensions.name: Pipeline decomposition & thresholds as milestones
dimensions.description: Breaking the work into ordered sub-goals (parse → metric implementation → baseline alignment → optimization) each with a concrete done-check tied to the score thresholds.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Two deliverables with distinct constraints and a multi-stage pipeline mean undifferentiated 'just write the file' effort will strand the agent without knowing whether it's close.

anchors.0: One undifferentiated push; no separable stages, no per-deliverable structure.
anchors.3: Implicit ordering only; treats both alignments as one blob and has no notion of intermediate checkpoints.
anchors.5: Separates parsing, scoring, and alignment generation, and tracks the two deliverables distinctly with their respective thresholds as goals.
anchors.8: Explicit ordered milestones (parser verified → S3/NC computable → baseline score measured → optimize to threshold) each with a numeric done-criterion, sequenced sensibly (e.g., build the scorer before optimizing against it).
anchors.10: A crisp milestone hierarchy that also budgets effort across the two deliverables by difficulty (the NC-constrained yeast task vs the S3-only fly task), with fallback branches per milestone and clear gating on measured scores before advancing.

dimensions.name: Self-scoring against the specified metrics
dimensions.description: Building/using a correct local implementation of S3 and NC (and injectivity/format checks) to measure alignments before trusting them.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The grader is hidden but the metrics are fully specified. An agent that cannot compute its own S3/NC is optimizing blind and cannot know if it passed; a subtly wrong scorer is worse than none.

anchors.0: Never computes S3 or NC; submits alignments hoping they pass.
anchors.3: Eyeballs coverage or computes a rough proxy, but no faithful S3/NC implementation; no format/injectivity validation.
anchors.5: Implements S3 and NC per the spec and runs them on its alignments, plus checks injectivity, full coverage of V1, and exact node-name/format matching.
anchors.8: Faithful metric implementation that it sanity-checks (e.g., scores the reference alignment to confirm NC≈1.0 and a sensible S3, tests edge cases like the E2_aligned denominator), and uses the score as the optimization objective/stopping test.
anchors.10: Rigorously validated scorer used as a tight feedback loop: cross-checks the S3 formula against the reference, guards against off-by-one/edge-set-double-counting bugs, verifies format matches the exact spec, and treats a passing local score as necessary-but-scrutinized rather than final.

dimensions.name: Score-tracking across optimization
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate picture of current S3/NC vs targets across iterations and detecting stalled or plateaued optimization.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Optimization can plateau below threshold; without tracking best-so-far scores the agent won't know if it's converging, stuck, or regressing across a long run.

anchors.0: No awareness of current scores or distance to thresholds; can't say whether it's improving.
anchors.3: Occasionally prints a number but no continuity — no sense of best-so-far or trend.
anchors.5: Tracks current S3/NC against each threshold and knows which deliverables still fall short.
anchors.8: Maintains best-so-far per deliverable across iterations, recognizes plateaus/regressions, and decides when an approach has stopped yielding gains rather than looping indefinitely.
anchors.10: Disciplined trajectory monitoring: logs score progression, distinguishes 'converging slowly' from 'stuck', avoids re-running variants that already failed, and preserves the best alignment while exploring — never loses the plot over a long optimization horizon.

dimensions.name: Strategy revision when thresholds aren't met
dimensions.description: Changing algorithm, parameters, or signal (topology vs name-overlap vs reference-seeding) when the current approach plateaus below target.
dimensions.why_it_matters: A first-choice method may not reach S3≥0.55/NC≥0.30; success often depends on switching or combining strategies rather than grinding the same one.

anchors.0: Keeps the same failing approach (or ships a below-threshold file) despite no progress.
anchors.3: Minor tweaks only (reruns with a different seed) without diagnosing why it fell short.
anchors.5: When stuck, tries a materially different tactic (new algorithm, added seeding, tuned objective) prompted by the observed shortfall.
anchors.8: Diagnoses the cause of the shortfall (e.g., NC low → exploit name-overlap/reference seeding; S3 low → local topological search) and pivots deliberately, keeping what worked.
anchors.10: Fluid, evidence-driven course-correction: forms hypotheses about why a metric lags, tests targeted changes, combines complementary signals for the two different constraint sets, and abandons dead ends quickly without discarding accumulated gains.
